annotationRationale: The decisive geometric fact identifies each hypotenuse as a diameter; the circle area formula then gives the ratio. The supplied routes all use this same argument.

review.questionCheck: An inscribed right triangle's hypotenuse is a diameter. The radii are 5/2 and 13/2, yielding area ratio 25/169, choice D. The stem and key agree, and no figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently verified and retained 2023_AMC_10B_Q03/hypotenuses-as-diameters. The LIVE explanation and supplied AoPS Solutions 1, 1.5, 2, and 3 all use the same diameter-and-area argument. Their radius, diameter, and similarity formulations are equivalent here; no additional method is beneficial.
review.annotationCheck: Both the diameter/right-angle relationship and circle area are central assessed concepts. The empty support and context lists are appropriate.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The converse diameter-angle theorem correctly identifies diameters 5 and 13. Substituting half these lengths into πr² and canceling common factors gives 25/169.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits 2023_AMC_10B_Q03/hypotenuses-as-diameters and retains both inherited LIVE and AoPS reference IDs. The supplied methodLocalSources supports project reuse. The source-informed-original basis is accurate, with no official MAA claim or copied third-party exposition.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: States the relevant standard circle theorem at use, connects it directly to the hypotenuses, and displays the complete area calculation. No material explanation or diagram is missing.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_254 explicitly includes the converse used here; cnm_p192 supplies the area formula. Both nodes precisely match the derivation.
